correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact zonoid normalization \(B^3=K(4\Theta)\), the published mixed-volume/random-determinant identity, an exact multilinear determinant identity checked on all basis tuples, and analytic spherical expectations \(\mathbb E\sin\Theta=\pi/4\) and \(\mathbb E|\cos\Theta|=1/2\). This gives \(W_{2,B^3}(1,1,1)=\pi^4/90\), hence \(W/|B^3|^2=\pi^2/160\). Affine covariance under \(T\oplus T\) extends the identity to every ellipsoid. No numerical experiment is used to establish an infinite statement.

value.rationale: The lead paper shows that \(W_{2,K}(1,1,1)\) is the only nontrivial higher-order coefficient remaining in dimension three and leaves its extremal equality structure unresolved. Ellipsoids form the canonical affine-smooth comparison class, so an exact normalized coefficient and its exact fraction \(\pi^2/48\) of the universal upper bound provide a natural calibration for that problem. The invariant is motivated before computation and is not an arbitrary slice or a known-table recomputation.
